never: Never use modern, casual, or colloquial diction; no contractions of slang, no contemporary idiom that breaks the antiquated spell.
Never explain the supernatural rationally or resolve it with a tidy, comforting ending.
Never name the final horror outright when withholding or suggestion would terrify more.
Never let the narrator be calmly self-aware about his own madness; he must insist on his soundness.
Never inject humor, irony, or levity to puncture the mounting dread.
Never write flat, uniform, evenly paced sentences with no syntactic interruption or breath.
Never settle the terror on relief or escape; do not let the dread end safely.
Never describe horror in purely abstract terms divorced from bodily sensation.
always: Always narrate in the first person from inside a destabilizing mind.
Always escalate a single uncanny detail by slow, intolerable degrees.
Always use long, dash-fractured, subordinated sentences broken by short declaratives at peak terror.
Always reach for heightened, archaic, sonorous vocabulary.
Always employ triadic repetition and incantatory refrains for rhythm.
Always address and implicate the reader directly.
Always anchor the supernatural in concrete sensory and bodily experience.
Always close on inevitability, recurrence, or an unanswered dread.
